question: Which of the following compounds does NOT belong to the homologous series of alcohols?
solution:
The correct answer is __**C4H10OH**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To determine which compound does not belong to the homologous series of alcohols, we first review the general formula and definition:
 
• Homologous Series of Alcohols:
 
• Alcohols belong to a homologous series with the general formula: CnH2n+1OH
 
• Each member differs from the next by -CH₂ gᵣₒᵤₚ.
 
• They all contain the hydroxyl functional group (–OH).
 
• C4H10OH
 
• For n=4 n=4, the formula should be:
 
 
• C4H10OH=C 4 ​ H 2(4)+1 ​ OH
 
• However, C4H10OH has one extra hydrogen atom and does not fit the alcohol homologous series.
 It is NOT a valid alcohol in the series.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **C3H7OH (Propanol):**

 
 
• Fits the general formula for n = 3: C3H2(3)+1OH
 
• **Valid alcohol**
 
 
 
• **CH3OH (Methanol):**
 
 
• Fits the general formula for n = 1: CH2(1)+1OH
 
 
• **Valid alcohol**
 
 
 
 
 
• **C2H5OH (Ethanol):**
 
 
• Fits the general formula for n = 2: C2H2(2)+1OH
 
• **Valid alcohol**
